Label quality scores

Source: R/scores.R
label_quality_scores.Rd

Scores how likely each given label is to be correct, from 0 (probably wrong) to 1 (probably right). Scores depend only on the predicted probabilities p of an example and its given label y (Kuan and Mueller, 2022):

  • "self_confidence": p[y], the predicted probability of the given label.

  • "normalized_margin": (p[y] - max(p[-y]) + 1) / 2, the gap between the given label and the most likely other class, rescaled to [0, 1]. Low when another class is clearly preferred.

  • "confidence_weighted_entropy": ratio / (1 + ratio) with ratio = p[y] / H(p), where H is the entropy of p divided by log(K). Also low for examples whose predictions are spread over many classes, such as examples that belong to none of the classes.

With adjust = TRUE, each class threshold t (see class_thresholds()) is subtracted from the predicted probabilities before scoring. This corrects for a classifier that systematically favours some classes. The adjusted probabilities are (p - t + max(t)) / sum(p - t + max(t)), which are non-negative and sum to one.

Usage

label_quality_scores(
  x,
  ...,
  method = c("self_confidence", "normalized_margin", "confidence_weighted_entropy"),
  adjust = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed to label_inputs(): for example pred_probs when x is a label vector, or truth when x is a data frame.

method

Scoring method, see Description.

adjust

Adjust predicted probabilities by the class thresholds before scoring? Not available for "confidence_weighted_entropy".

Value

A numeric vector with one score per example, in the order of label_inputs(x, ...)$row_id.

References

Kuan, J., & Mueller, J. (2022). Model-agnostic label quality scoring to detect real-world label errors. ICML DataPerf Workshop. doi:10.5281/zenodo.18168246

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 300, seed = 1)
scores <- label_quality_scores(sim, truth = given)
# Mislabelled examples get lower scores
tapply(scores, sim$given != sim$true, mean)
#>     FALSE      TRUE 
#> 0.6094508 0.1968347
